“These are troubles that have besieged me,’ he therefore said to himself. ‘Evils
have come upon me in succession, and trials have surrounded me. Yet I still have my intelligence: my situation should not frighten me, nor
my affair should terrify me, perplexity overtake me, nor should I be disheartened.

The sensible man does not lose
his judgement, and his mind does not abandon him, whatever the circumstance;

for intelligence resembles the sea whose deeps cannot be reached.
The

p.n: Situations Do Not Blind the Intelligent

body.p:
level-headed man does not remain exhausted; and one should not allow one’s disposition to reach the point where one becomes blind
to one’s situation.

p.n: The Rat Decides on a Pact with the Cat

body.p:
I see no way out for me from this trouble except reconciliation with the cat, for he
has been beset by the same trouble that has beset me-or part thereof. Perhaps, if he listens to my words, which I shall address him
with, and heed my eloquent address and pure sincerity, about which there is no disagreement and with which comes no deceit,
he will understand it and desiremy help to him, thus delivering us together.’”

p.n: The Rat Comes Up to the Cat

body.p:
“And so the rat approached the cat
and said, ‘How are you?’
‘As you would like,’ he said, ‘in dire straits!’ ‘And today,

p.n: The Rat Points Out Their Common Problem

body.p:
I’m your partner in trouble,’ he said.
‘I can only hope to be delivered through hoping that you similarly be delivered.
These words of mine contain no lie or deceitfulness.

The mongoose, here, is lying in ambush for me,
and the owl is watching me, and both, to you and me, are enemies. So if you provide me with safety, I shall cut
your bonds and deliver you from this trouble. If that happens, either one shall be delivered
by the other- as with

p.n: Sailors Depend on Ships and Vice Versa

body.p: a ship and its passengers at sea: by the ship they are delivered and by them
